title: Data-anchoring profiles and automated attestation export
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add a first-class 'data-anchoring' profile concept to the Hosted API so tenants can declare preferred residency constraints and retention rules; implement server-side enforcement for routing and a certifiable attestation export that packages regional routing decisions, retention settings, and associated audit logs for customer compliance reviews. This ticket owns the product spec, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and coordination with Eng and Design for the UX and export format.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can create and save named data-anchoring profiles that include: allowed regions (ordered), retention policy (TTL tiers), and enforcement mode (soft / hard)
Console UI allows assigning a profile to an existing API key or tenant with clear indicators for soft/hard enforcement and estimated impact on latency/cost
Routing layer respects hard enforcement profiles (requests are routed to pinned regions or rejected/fallback according to policy) within existing policy orchestration SLOs

Automated attestation export generates a signed bundle (JSON + signed manifest) containing: effective profile, route history for the last 90 days, retention-rule snapshots, and relevant audit log slices; bundle can be downloaded from Console and via API
Attestation export includes verifiable evidence (timestamps, request IDs, region tags) and links to relevant logs in the audit store; format documented in Confluence
Upgrade path for tenants: existing region preferences are migrated to a default profile without disrupting current traffic
E2E tests and an acceptance harness validate routing behavior under soft vs hard modes and verify exported bundles for completeness and signature validity

decisions: Use a named profile model rather than ad-hoc per-endpoint pins to simplify audits and rollbacks
Export bundle format: JSON manifest + gzipped log slice + detached signature (PKCS7) to support both automated ingestion and human review
Default enforcement mode for migrated tenants: 'soft' to avoid unexpected request failures; explicit opt-in required for 'hard' enforcement
Retention tiers will default to 30/90/365 days with an escape hatch for regulatory overrides via support request
notes: Rollout plan: feature flag + beta for 10 pilot tenants, gather evidence bundle samples, then GA after security sign-off
Monitoring: add per-profile routing rejection metric, per-profile export success/failure counter, and attestation bundle generation latency
Backfill strategy: for tenants that opt-in to hard mode, run a staged verification window before switching enforcement and emit a preflight attestation
